home.manifestoLead: We plan the way a local would — slowly, and with one person in mind.
home.signatureTitle: A planner, not a call centre

experiences.title: Sigiriya Village Tour
experiences.copy: Ride a bullock cart, cross the lake by catamaran, walk through paddy fields, learn traditional cooking and share a village lunch.

experiences.title: Tea Plantation & Tea Plucking Experience
experiences.copy: Wear a tea picker’s basket, pluck fresh leaves, follow them through a working tea factory and finish with a cup of Ceylon tea.

experiences.title: Whale & Dolphin Watching
experiences.copy: Set out on an early-morning boat safari in search of blue whales, sperm whales and pods of dolphins in Sri Lanka’s offshore waters.

experiences.title: White Water Rafting
experiences.copy: Run the Kelani River’s forest-framed rapids with an experienced guide, with routes suited to both first-time and experienced rafters.

experiences.title: Spice Garden Experience
experiences.copy: Walk through a spice plantation, discover the uses of Ayurvedic herbs and see how Sri Lanka’s familiar spices are grown and prepared.

experiences.title: Pinnawala Elephant Experience
experiences.copy: Observe elephants during river bathing and feeding sessions while learning about their care, behaviour and ongoing conservation.

experiences.title: Kandy Cultural Dance Show
experiences.copy: Experience Kandyan drumming, ceremonial dance, vivid traditional costumes and the dramatic fire-walking finale in the heart of Kandy.

experiences.title: Sea Turtle Conservation Farm Visit
experiences.copy: Visit a coastal hatchery, meet rescued sea turtles and learn how local conservation teams protect nests and support their release.

experiences.title: Traditional Sri Lankan Cooking Class
experiences.copy: Shop at a local market, prepare authentic curries and sambols with a host, then sit down together to enjoy the meal you made.

experiences.title: Yala or Udawalawe Jeep Safari
experiences.copy: Travel by private jeep in search of elephants, crocodiles and exotic birdlife, with chances to see leopards and sloth bears in Yala.

experiences.title: Scenic Train Journey
experiences.copy: Ride Sri Lanka’s celebrated hill-country railway through tea estates, cloud forest and mountain villages between Kandy, Nuwara Eliya and Ella.

experiences.title: Catamaran Sunset Cruise
experiences.copy: Unwind aboard a catamaran in Bentota, Trincomalee or Mirissa as the coastline softens into the evening light.

experiences.title: Fishing with Local Fishermen
experiences.copy: Join local fishermen on the coast, try traditional techniques and discover the working rhythms of Sri Lanka’s fishing villages.

experiences.title: Ayurvedic Wellness & Spa
experiences.copy: Slow down with herbal treatments, therapeutic massage and personalised wellness rituals rooted in Sri Lanka’s Ayurvedic traditions.

experiences.title: Cycling Through Rural Villages
experiences.copy: Follow quiet lanes past paddy fields, temples and lakes, meeting local communities along the way on a guided bicycle tour.

about.heroAlt: A path through the Sri Lankan forest
about.intro: We started ReiseCeylon to share Sri Lanka with the care, nuance and humanity it deserves.
about.quote: The best journeys do not make a place feel consumed. They make it feel understood.
about.copy: Our team brings together local travel designers, hosts, naturalists and storytellers. We work with independent stays and responsible partners, choosing depth over volume and lasting relationships over quick transactions.
about.card1Copy: Decisions are made here, with knowledge shaped by seasons and lived experience.
about.card2Copy: We recommend fewer places and know them more deeply.
about.card3Copy: Your journey should benefit the people and landscapes that make it possible.
about.approachCopy1: We begin with the season, the time you have and the places that genuinely suit your interests. Then we look at road time, opening days and the natural rhythm between coast, hills, heritage and wildlife.
about.approachCopy2: Nothing is added only to make an itinerary look busy. We leave room for rest, conversation and unexpected stops, while working with people and small businesses that know their region well.
about.approachCopy3: Before you travel, we review the route again for seasonal conditions and practical changes. This keeps the plan realistic while protecting the sense of discovery that brought you to Sri Lanka.

contact.intro: Share a little about the trip in your mind. A Sri Lanka travel designer will reply {responseTime} with thoughtful first ideas.
contact.guidanceCopy1: Tell us your travel dates, group size, preferred pace and the parts of Sri Lanka that interest you. It is also useful to share any mobility, dietary or room needs from the start.
contact.guidanceCopy2: You do not need a finished itinerary. We will turn those details into a practical first route, explain the main choices and adjust it with you before anything is confirmed.
contact.guidanceCopy3: If you already have flights or a list of places, include them in your message. We can check whether the route is comfortable, where longer drives may occur and which stops work well together. Clear details at the beginning help us reply with advice that is useful for your actual trip.
contact.guidanceCopy4: Every enquiry is reviewed by a person. Your first reply will explain the next practical step, and there is no obligation to book.

faq.seasonQuestion: When is the best time to visit {name}?
faq.seasonAnswerSouthwest: {name} follows Sri Lanka's southwestern weather pattern: driest from December to April, with the southwest monsoon bringing the heaviest rain between May and September.
faq.seasonAnswerNortheast: {name} follows Sri Lanka's northeastern and dry-zone weather pattern: driest from May to September, with the northeast monsoon bringing the heaviest rain between October and January.
faq.seasonAnswerBoth: Because the island runs two monsoons on opposite coasts, some part of Sri Lanka is in season in every month of the year.

faq.nearbyAnswerCaveat: Those distances are straight-line, so the drive is always longer.

blog.intro: Local perspective, unrushed guides and ideas for seeing Sri Lanka with greater depth.
blog.guideTitle: Useful Sri Lanka travel stories, written from the island.
blog.guideCopy1: Our field notes help you understand a place before adding it to a route. We cover practical timing, cultural context, wildlife etiquette, train journeys, regional food and the small choices that can make a visit calmer and more rewarding.
blog.guideCopy2: Each article is researched for travellers planning a private Sri Lanka journey. Use these stories to compare regions, choose the right season and ask better questions. When details such as opening times or access rules can change, we check them again while planning your trip.
blog.guideCopy3: You will also find honest explanations of travel distances and pace. Sri Lanka looks small on a map, but mountain roads, rail journeys and worthwhile pauses shape each day. Understanding that rhythm early helps you build a route with fewer rushed stops and more time to experience the places you chose.
blog.guideCopy4: The aim is not to publish a checklist of attractions. We want each guide to answer a real planning question and show how a place fits into a wider journey. New notes are added as our team revisits routes, speaks with local partners and learns what travellers need before they arrive.
